name: Mittlere Jass
description: Mittlere Jass is an unusual Swiss Jass game for three players. It is a point trick game where the basic objective is to avoid ending up with the middle score. The game features dynamic trump determination - the first suit played that cannot be followed becomes trumps for the rest of the hand. It is played with sticks (which players try to win) and potatoes (which players try to avoid).

history.origins: Mittlere Jass is a Swiss Jass variant, part of the larger Jass family that originated in the Netherlands and became extremely popular in Switzerland. The game was documented by Nick Wedd in English-language card game literature.
timeline: Traditional: Developed within Swiss Jass tradition
Modern: Documented and shared through Jass-playing communities
Present: Played by Jass enthusiasts, particularly those seeking three-player options
history.cultural: Jass is the national card game of Switzerland, played in pubs, clubs, and homes throughout the country. Mittlere offers a unique three-player option in a game family often optimized for four.
history.evolution: The game is the three-player ancestor of Molotow Jass (for four players). The unique middle-score objective distinguishes it from other Jass games.

setup.deck: 36-card Jass deck (6 through Ace in four suits: Acorns, Shields, Flowers, Bells). Can use standard deck with 5s and below removed.
setup.dealing: All 36 cards dealt out, 12 to each player, in packets of 3. Deal and play are anticlockwise.
setup.equipment: 36-card Jass deck or modified standard deck, scoring slate (for sticks and potatoes).

rules.objective: Avoid having the middle score. Score points by winning tricks, but avoid being caught in the middle.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads to first trick. Must follow suit if possible. If unable to follow, may play any card - if no trump is established, this card's suit becomes trumps. Once trump is established, must follow suit or trump if void.
keyRules: Sticks are good, potatoes are bad

strategy.basic: Try to win either many points (79-99 is safe) or very few points (under 29 is safe). Avoid the middle range. Ensure you win at least one trick.
strategy.intermediate: Control when trumps are established by choosing when to void yourself. Win early tricks to control the lead. Preserve 6s (guaranteed exits) and Aces.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential. Track suit distribution to predict when trumps will be established. Coordinate (without explicit communication) to force opponents into the middle. Calculate risk ranges based on cards played.
tips: 79-99 points guarantees a stick (others have less)
Under 29 points guarantees a stick (someone has 100+ or no tricks)
Win at least one trick or you get 2 potatoes
Leading short suits increases chance of establishing favorable trumps

scoring.description: Scoring uses sticks (positive) and potatoes (negative). Check scoring conditions in priority order and apply only the first that applies.
scoring.winCondition: After 12 hands, player with most sticks (or fewest potatoes) wins.
